newsitem.title: USA: Republican Senate leader - budget accord reached.
newsitem.headline: Republican Senate leader - budget accord reached.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott told reporters Thursday a balanced budget agreement has been reached with the White House and will be brought for a vote in the Senate Budget Committee Monday.

"Yes, we have an agreement. It's over," the Mississippi Republican said. The plan calls for balanced budget by the year 2002. It provides for a net $85 billion tax cut over five years including President Clinton's $35 billion five-year tax credit for education.

Lott said the budget deal also includes an automatic extension in the U.S. debt ceiling to provide enough authority to carry the government's borrowing needs through Dec. 15, 1999. This change takes the contentious debt ceiling increase out of the politics of the 1998 election.

The House Budget Committee has scheduled its discussion of the budget proposal for Friday at 10 a.m. EDT (1400 GMT). The congressional leaders aim to seek final approval in both the full House and Senate before the May 23 recess for the Memorial Day holiday.

White House Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles and other top White House officials were closeted with Republican leaders most of the day in the office of House Speaker Newt Gingrich, Republican of Georgia, working out last minute snags. The deal had originally been announced May 2, but lacked specifics and led to nearly two weeks of wrangling over details.

The budget forms the blueprint for tax and spending policies for the next five years. It does not require President Clinton's signature but was negotiated with him to ease passage of legislation that will enact the tax cuts and spending cuts needed to reduce the deficit to zero by 2002.
